text: The case concerns the alleged lack of public access to a reasoned judgment in a civil case.
The case concerns the applicant's arrest and administrative offence proceedings for participating in an unlawful public assembly.
The case concerns the applicant's dismissal from the police for criticising her superiors.
The applicant was born in 1967.
The applicant lives in Moscow.
The applicant had been granted legal aid.
The applicant was represented by Ms V. Petrova, a lawyer practising in Moscow.
The Government were represented by Mr G. Matyushkin, Representative of the Russian Federation to the European Court of Human Rights.
Mr G. Matyushkin was succeeded in the office of Representative of the Russian Federation to the European Court of Human Rights by Mr M. Galperin.
The Government were subsequently represented by Mr M. Galperin, Representative of the Russian Federation to the European Court of Human Rights.
The facts of the case, as submitted by the parties, may be summarised as follows.
The applicant was a police officer in the Administrative Department of the Special Police Force (ОМОН).
section_path: I. SOLO DEMONSTRATION OF 25 FEBRUARY 2009 AND THE APPLICANT'S DISMISSAL FROM POLICE SERVICE

text: On 25 February 2009 the applicant held a solo demonstration in front of the Government of Russia building.
section_path: I. SOLO DEMONSTRATION OF 25 FEBRUARY 2009 AND THE APPLICANT'S DISMISSAL FROM POLICE SERVICE

text: The applicant's solo demonstration of 25 February 2009 was covered by the press.
section_path: I. SOLO DEMONSTRATION OF 25 FEBRUARY 2009 AND THE APPLICANT'S DISMISSAL FROM POLICE SERVICE

text: The applicant alleged that the in-house police medical practitioner had damaged her daughter's health on purpose.
section_path: I. SOLO DEMONSTRATION OF 25 FEBRUARY 2009 AND THE APPLICANT'S DISMISSAL FROM POLICE SERVICE

text: On 13 March 2009 the applicant was dismissed from the police for a serious breach of disciplinary rules.
section_path: I. SOLO DEMONSTRATION OF 25 FEBRUARY 2009 AND THE APPLICANT'S DISMISSAL FROM POLICE SERVICE

text: On 24 March 2009 the applicant challenged her dismissal before the Tverskoy District Court of Moscow.
section_path: I. SOLO DEMONSTRATION OF 25 FEBRUARY 2009 AND THE APPLICANT'S DISMISSAL FROM POLICE SERVICE

text: On 10 April 2009 the Tverskoy District Court found it established that by holding the solo demonstration the applicant had committed a serious breach of disciplinary rules.
section_path: I. SOLO DEMONSTRATION OF 25 FEBRUARY 2009 AND THE APPLICANT'S DISMISSAL FROM POLICE SERVICE

text: On 10 April 2009 the Tverskoy District Court found that there had been statutory grounds for the applicant's dismissal.
section_path: I. SOLO DEMONSTRATION OF 25 FEBRUARY 2009 AND THE APPLICANT'S DISMISSAL FROM POLICE SERVICE

text: On 10 April 2009 the Tverskoy District Court found that the applicant's dismissal had been lawful.
section_path: I. SOLO DEMONSTRATION OF 25 FEBRUARY 2009 AND THE APPLICANT'S DISMISSAL FROM POLICE SERVICE

text: On 30 June 2010 the Moscow City Court upheld the Tverskoy District Court judgment of 10 April 2009 on appeal.
section_path: I. SOLO DEMONSTRATION OF 25 FEBRUARY 2009 AND THE APPLICANT'S DISMISSAL FROM POLICE SERVICE

text: On 30 June 2010 the Moscow City Court found that the Tverskoy District Court judgment of 10 April 2009 had been lawful, sufficiently reasoned and justified.
section_path: I. SOLO DEMONSTRATION OF 25 FEBRUARY 2009 AND THE APPLICANT'S DISMISSAL FROM POLICE SERVICE

text: On 20 September 2010 the applicant notified the Prefect of the Central Administrative District of Moscow of her intention to hold a picket from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. on 23 September 2010.
The intended picket on 23 September 2010 was to be held in front of the Prosecutor General's office on Bolshaya Dmitrovka Street.
Ten people were expected to attend the intended picket on 23 September 2010.
The aim of the intended picket on 23 September 2010 was to draw the Prosecutor General's attention to corruption of prosecutors and to the absence of any effective remedy in that respect.
On 20 September 2010 the Prefect of the Central Administrative District of Moscow refused to approve the public event planned for 23 September 2010.

The Prefect of the Central Administrative District of Moscow refused to approve the public event on the ground that the notification had been submitted outside the time-limit established by the Public Events Act (no. FZ-54 of 19 June 2004).
At about 10.20 a.m. on 23 September 2010 four people started to picket on Bolshaya Dmitrovka Street in front of the Prosecutor General's office.
As it was raining on 23 September 2010, the participants to the picket took shelter in the archway of one of the neighbouring buildings.
The participants to the picket on 23 September 2010 displayed placards protesting against corruption of prosecutors.
At about 11 a.m. on 23 September 2010 the participants to the picket were arrested by the police and brought to a police station.
The applicant was released at 2 p.m. on 23 September 2010.

On 11 November 2010 the Justice of the Peace of the 369th Court Circuit of the Tverskoy District of Moscow found the applicant guilty of a breach of the established procedure for the conduct of public events, an offence under Article 20.2 § 1 of the Administrative Offences Code.
The Justice of the Peace of the 369th Court Circuit of the Tverskoy District of Moscow found that the applicant had organised a public event which had not received an official approval.
The Justice of the Peace of the 369th Court Circuit of the Tverskoy District of Moscow sentenced the applicant to a fine in the amount of 1,000 Russian roubles (about 23.5 euros).
The applicant appealed against the judgment of 11 November 2010 of the Justice of the Peace of the 369th Court Circuit of the Tverskoy District of Moscow.

The applicant argued on appeal that she had submitted a notification on 20 September 2010, that is three days before the intended event of 23 September 2010, as required by the Public Events Act (no. FZ-54 of 19 June 2004).
The applicant argued on appeal that the Prefect of the Central Administrative District of Moscow's refusal to approve the event had been unlawful.
On 28 December 2010 the Tverskoy District Court upheld the judgment of 11 November 2010 of the Justice of the Peace of the 369th Court Circuit of the Tverskoy District of Moscow on appeal.

The Tverskoy District Court found on appeal that the notification for the event had been submitted at 11.25 a.m. on 20 September 2010, that is less than three days before the intended event which had been scheduled to start at 10 a.m. on 23 September 2010.
The Tverskoy District Court found on appeal that the applicant had not complied with the time-limit established by the Public Events Act (no. FZ-54 of 19 June 2004).
The Tverskoy District Court found on appeal that the Prefect of the Central Administrative District of Moscow's refusal to approve the event had been lawful.

The Tverskoy District Court found on appeal that by holding a public event which had not received an official approval, the applicant had violated the established procedure for the conduct of public events.
The applicant sued the Moscow Interior Department for a long-service pension payable to police officers after twenty years of service.
On 6 August 2009 the Tverskoy District Court held a hearing in the pension dispute between the applicant and the Moscow Interior Department.
At the close of the hearing on 6 August 2009, the Tverskoy District Court read out the operative part of the judgment, stating that the applicant's claims were dismissed in full.
A copy of the reasoned judgment of 6 August 2009 was served on the applicant on 31 August 2009.
The applicant appealed against the Tverskoy District Court judgment of 6 August 2009.
The applicant complained on appeal that the Tverskoy District Court had not read out the full text of the judgment at the hearing of 6 August 2009.
On 14 September 2010 the Moscow City Court held an appeal hearing in the pension dispute.

At the close of the appeal hearing on 14 September 2010, the Moscow City Court read out the operative part of the judgment, stating that the Tverskoy District Court judgment of 6 August 2009 was upheld.
On 26 January 2011 the applicant received a copy of the Moscow City Court appeal judgment of 14 September 2010.
The Moscow City Court appeal judgment of 14 September 2010 did not address the issue of public pronouncement of the first-instance and appeal judgments.
The Public Events Act (no. FZ-54 of 19 June 2004) provides that a notification in respect of a picket involving several persons must be submitted no later than three days before the intended picket.

The Public Events Act (no. FZ-54 of 19 June 2004) provides that if the end of the notification time-limit falls on a Sunday or a public holiday, the notification must be submitted no later than four days before the intended picket.
The Public Events Act (no. FZ-54 of 19 June 2004) provides that no notification is required for gatherings or pickets involving one person (section 7 paragraphs 1 and 3).
Article 191 of the Civil Code of the Russian Federation provides that a time-limit starts to run on the next day after the date, or the occurrence of the event, which sets off its beginning.

Ruling no. 28 by the Plenary Supreme Court of 26 June 2018 provides that the day when the notification is lodged and the day when the public event is scheduled to take place are not taken into account for the calculation of the notification time-limit (paragraph 6).

For a complete summary of the domestic provisions on the procedure for the notification and conduct of public events and liability for breaches committed in the course of public events, see Lashmankin and Others v. Russia (nos. 57818/09 and 14 others, §§ 216-312, 7 February 2017).
Article 199 §§ 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure (as in force at the material time) provided that a judgment was to be delivered immediately after the examination of a case.
Article 199 §§ 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure (as in force at the material time) provided that the operative part of the judgment was to be pronounced at the last hearing.

Article 199 §§ 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure (as in force at the material time) provided that the pronounced operative part of the judgment was to be signed by all judges and included in the case file.
Article 199 §§ 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure (as in force at the material time) provided that the preparation of a reasoned judgment could be postponed for no more than five days.

The Courts Administration Office's Instruction no. 36 of 29 April 2003 (in force at the material time) set out an exhaustive list of persons who were allowed to consult a case file in a court building, including the parties to the proceedings, their representatives, other participants to the proceedings, public prosecutors and other officials (paragraph 12.1).

The Courts Administration Office's Instruction no. 36 of 29 April 2003 (in force at the material time) set out an exhaustive list of persons who could be given copies of documents from a case file, including the parties to the proceedings and their representatives (paragraph 12.6).
Federal Law no. 262-FZ of 22 December 2008 on Access to Information on the Functioning of Courts in the Russian Federation provided for the publication of domestic courts' judgments on the internet.
Federal Law no. 262-FZ of 22 December 2008 on Access to Information on the Functioning of Courts in the Russian Federation came into force on 1 July 2010.
For a summary of other provisions concerning the public pronouncement of judgments, see Malmberg and Others v. Russia, nos. 23045/05 and 3 others, §§ 30-41, 15 January 2015.
